signal.title: [core][joblib] Add opt-in autoscaling to ray.util.multiprocessing.Pool
signal.text: ## Description Closes #31128. The Ray joblib backend is built on `ray.util.multiprocessing.Pool`, which historically created a fixed actor pool from the cluster's current CPU count. That prevents a zero-CPU head from expressing a larger logical concurrency target and scaling workers from zero. This PR adds an experimental, opt-in autoscaling mode to the existing Pool. Supplying any of `min_size`, `max_size`, `initial_size`, or `idle_timeout_s` enables it; `Pool()` and `Pool(processes=N)` retain fixed-pool mode. ```python pool = Pool( min_size=0, max_size=64, initial_size=0, idle_timeout_s=60, ray_remote_args={"num_cpus": 1}, ) ``` Pool autoscaling and cluster autoscaling are separate. Pool actors still use their existing `num_cpus=0` default. Callers must explicitly request resources through `ray_remote_args` when pending actors should create Ray autoscaler demand. The default joblib backend forwards the same options at backend construction: ```python register_ray() with joblib.parallel_backend( "ray", n_jobs=8, max_size=8, initial_size=0, ray_remote_args={"num_cpus": 1}, ): ... ``` `register_ray()` only registers the backend; it does not store Pool defaults. ## Design One dispatcher thread owns actor lifecycle and scheduling state: 1. `starting` actors carry resource demand but receive no work. 2. A successful `__ray_ready__` ObjectRef moves an actor to `ready`. 3. A ready actor receives one batch and becomes `running`. 4. Batch completion returns it to `ready`; actor death clears its slot so the resize step can replace it. 5. Idle ready actors are reaped down to `min_size`. ObjectRef callbacks only wake the dispatcher. They do not mutate Pool state. Pending actors therefore cannot strand work that can run on already-ready actors when `max_size` exceeds current cluster capacity. Fixed and autoscaling modes share lifecycle code, but preserve different scheduling properties: - fixed mode keeps the eager readiness barrier and historical balanced batch distribution; - autoscaling mode is work-conserving and never waits for pending capacity while a ready actor can serve work. Startup submission/readiness failures share a bounded retry budget and retry deadline. Ordinary batch completion does not reset that budget. Unexpected dispatcher or ResultThread exceptions are converted into result errors rather than silently terminating a background thread and stranding callers. ## Compatibility and scope - Autoscaling is opt-in; actor resource requirements never change implicitly. - `n_jobs` remains joblib's concurrency limit; `max_size` can lower but not raise it. - Fixed-pool actor crashes are now detected and replaced. - This uses the existing joblib/`multiprocessing.Pool` backend rather than adding a second task backend. - The API remains experimental and needs maintainer confirmation on final abstraction/layering. ## Validation Latest local validation used Ray 2.52.0 runtime wheels with the PR Python sources, Python 3.10/3.11, and both the repository-pinned joblib 1.2.0 and joblib 1.5.3. - State-machine fault injection: readiness, synchronous actor/method submission, per-actor startup failure accounting, bounded retry deadlines, actor death, dispatcher failure, and ResultThread `wait`/`get` failure all passed. - `test_joblib_autoscale.py`: isolated real-Ray failure/concurrency scenarios passed after the latest changes, including initializer failure, serialization failures, callback exception identity, actor replacement, close/terminate races, recycling, ready-actor death, and mixed concurrent submissions. - Zero-CPU-head `AutoscalingCluster` end-to-end passed and scaled 0 -> 8 CPUs. - Ray-side `test_multiprocessing.py` behavior passed; fixed-pool distribution was repeated five times and remained balanced (`28/28/23/21` for the existing 100-item case). - Standalone multiprocessing coverage passed for automatic Ray init, `maxtasksperchild`, and recursive-task deadlock avoidance. - joblib 1.2.0 core coverage passed for registration, sklearn/SVM and cross-validation, `ray_remote_args`, task assignment, and effective job counts. - joblib 1.2.0 and 1.5.3 both passed autoscaling serialization/error reuse and `n_jobs` concurrency tests. - `pre-commit run --files python/ray/util/multiprocessing/pool.py python/ray/tests/test_joblib_autoscale.py` passed. - `git diff --check` passed. The standard Bazel target was also invoked locally. It analyzed and built, but its bare local sandbox lacked NumPy and stopped during test import; the Ray CI image supplies the Python test dependencies, so the newly triggered PR CI is the authoritative standard-suite run. ## Duplicate-work check Open issues and PRs were checked before development. #31128 is the existing request; no competing implementation was found. #64959 is a duplicate design tracker created during development. ## AI assistance and human accountability AI assistance was used to develop and test this change. - [ ] The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and can defend the final design and implementation. - [ ] The human submitter has independently confirmed the final test results before requesting maintainer review. This PR remains a draft until both items are complete.

signal.title: [Core] Fix Windows fatal access violation during ActorPool teardown with runtime_env (Fixes #62442)
signal.text: ## Why are these changes needed? Fixes #62442 When an `ActorPool` is initialized on Windows with a `runtime_env` (such as `worker_process_setup_hook`), the worker processes crash with a "Windows fatal exception: access violation" during teardown. **Root Cause:** During process exit on Windows, the `atexit` sequence invokes `ray._private.worker.disconnect()`. This function attempts to read `worker.job_logging_config`, which reaches into the Cython bindings to call `CCoreWorkerProcess::GetCoreWorker()->GetJobConfig()`. Because Windows C++ static destructors run non-deterministically during process exit, the global `CoreWorker` pointer is frequently already invalidated, causing a hard memory access violation (segfault). **Solution:** Added a defensive check in `disconnect()` inside `worker.py`. If the python interpreter is actively exiting (`exiting_interpreter=True`) on `win32`, we bypass the `job_logging_config` check entirely, preventing the C++ pointer dereference and allowing the process to terminate cleanly. ## Related issue number Fixes #62442 ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit(by using the -s flag, i.e., `git commit -s`) in this PR. - [x] I've run `scripts/format.sh` to lint the changes in this PR. - [x] I've included any doc changes needed for https://docs.ray.io/en/master/. - [x] I've made sure the tests are passing. - [x] Testing Strategy: Added `test_actorpool_windows_crash.py` to natively verify the shutdown sequence doesn't segfault.

signal.title: [Data] Style and grammar pass on the Ray Data shuffle pages
signal.text: ## Summary Style and grammar pass across the Ray Data shuffle pages, measured against `doc/source/ray-contribute/writing-style.md`. Originally scoped to `data-internals.rst`; extended after #65372 merged so the shuffle v2 content it introduced gets the same treatment as the rest of the page, along with the sibling pages that reference it. No behavior claims are changed. Where a wording fix would have restated a technical claim I couldn't verify, I left the original text alone. ## Rendering fix `joining-data.rst` had three join-type lists written as: ```rst **Semi Joins:** - Left Semi, Right Semi (returns all rows ... ``` RST needs a blank line before a bullet list, so all three rendered as run-together paragraphs with literal `-` characters rather than lists. Confirmed with docutils before and after. ## Style fixes - **Sentence-case headings** throughout. Nothing catches these: `Google.Headings` is disabled repo-wide. - **Feature-stage casing.** "currently in Alpha" to "in alpha", per the guide's rule that Ray-owned stages are lowercase. - **Time-relative words.** Dropped "currently"; replaced the "this is a new feature released in Ray 2.46" note, since 2.46 is no longer new. - **Units.** "100 KB" to 100 KiB and "8 KB" to 8 KiB in `data-internals.rst`, matching the actual `100 * 1024` and `8192` values. The same section already said 1 GiB correctly. - **Bold-as-heading** to definition-list form for the two shuffle v2 tuning settings. - **`export`** added to the `RAY_DATA_DEFAULT_SHUFFLE_STRATEGY` snippet, and the variable named in the lead-in, so the snippet does what the prose describes. - **Wording.** "knobs" to "settings", "only applies" to "applies only", "group-bys" to "group-by operations", one spelling of "trade-off". - **Mechanical.** Unicode quotes and apostrophes, trailing whitespace, comma splices, missing terminal periods, and single backticks where surrounding text uses double. ## Note for reviewers Sentence-casing headings changes their generated HTML anchors, so any external deep link to, for example, `#basic-aggregations` still resolves but `#Custom-Aggregations`-style links to the old casing would not. `autosectionlabel` isn't enabled and every `:ref:` on these pages uses an explicit label, so no in-tree cross-reference breaks. Happy to revert the heading changes if the anchor churn isn't worth it. ## Follow-up A separate PR will carry the factual corrections these pages need, which are out of scope for a wording pass: - `saving-data.rst` sets `DataContext.shuffle_strategy` on the class rather than on `DataContext.get_current()`, which replaces the property descriptor instead of calling its setter. - `joining-data.rst` describes `partition_size_hint` as optional with a default and tuning guidance, but it's deprecated and ignored with no effect. - `joining-data.rst` says the aggregator count "defaults to 64". It's `min(num_partitions, min(ceil(cluster_CPUs), max_hash_shuffle_aggregators or 128))`.

signal.title: [Data] Add `max_concurrent_calls_per_actor` to ActorPoolStrategy
signal.text: ### Description This PR adds `max_concurrent_calls_per_actor` to `ActorPoolStrategy`. It controls how many calls can run concurrently on each actor. Ray Data passes this value to Ray Core as `max_concurrency`. This option belongs in `ActorPoolStrategy` because it only applies to actor workers. It is different from `max_tasks_in_flight_per_actor`, which controls how much work Ray Data can send to an actor. Example: ```python ray.data.ActorPoolStrategy( size=4, max_concurrent_calls_per_actor=8, ) ``` --- Closes https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/65529 Follow-up to #65228

signal.title: [Data] High-memory detector can report stale dynamic memory requests
signal.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen `HighMemoryIssueDetector` calls `MapOperator._get_dynamic_ray_remote_args()` when the detector is initialized and stores the returned `memory` value. During periodic detection, it calls the function again but compares memory usage against the value saved during initialization. ### Versions / Dependencies on `master` ### Reproduction script Configure a map operator with static `memory=1 GiB` and a `ray_remote_args_fn` that returns `memory=10 GiB`. If average worker memory usage is 8 GiB, periodic detection can compare the usage with the 1 GiB value captured earlier and emit a warning even though the current dynamic request is 10 GiB. ### Issue Severity None
signal.author: viiccwen

signal.title: [core][rdt] Application-level exclusive NIC assignment for NIXL/UCX t…
signal.text: ## Why Ray actors using RDT/NIXL over UCX don't control which RDMA NIC they use —UCX picks devices on its own. On multi-NIC nodes this means several actors can silently pile onto the same NIC while others sit idle, causing unpredictable tensor-transfer performance with no visible error. Closes/Addresses #64426. ## What Per discussion on the issue (thanks @Sparks0219 @stephanie-wang), this implements NIC pinning entirely at the application level inside `ray.experimental.rdt` — no Ray Core / scheduler / resource-model changes.This keeps the change small, fully opt-in, and iterable, while leaving the door open to promote parts of it into core later if the design holds up. ### `ray/experimental/rdt/nic_allocator.py` (new) - `discover_rdma_nics()` — enumerates port-qualified RDMA device names (e.g. `mlx5_0:1`) from `/sys/class/infiniband`, the same sysfs surface `_is_efa_available()` already relies on (works inside containers/pods where netdevs are namespaced away). Returns `[]` on non-RDMA/non-Linux hosts. - `NICAllocator` — a small `@ray.remote` actor acting as a cluster-wide registry of `(node, NIC) -> owning actor`. Runs as a single detached singleton; single-threaded actor execution gives us race-free acquire/release for free. Supports idempotent node registration, re-entrant acquisition (an actor re-acquiring gets the same NIC back instead of leaking a second one), and a `snapshot()` for observability. - `acquire_nic_for_current_actor()` / `release_nic_for_current_actor()` — the public entry points. Both are no-ops unless `RAY_RDT_NIC_PINNING=1` is set, and fail open on any error (discovery failure, allocator unreachable, timeout) by returning `None` / logging-and-returning, so a broken allocator degrades to today's behavior rather than breaking transfers. ### `ray/experimental/rdt/nixl_tensor_transport.py` `_init_nixl_agent()` now calls `acquire_nic_for_current_actor()` and, if it gets a NIC back, sets `UCX_NET_DEVICES` **before** constructing the NIXL agent (UCX reads this at context-init time). Scoped to the `UCX` backend only — `LIBFABRIC`/EFA is untouched. A user-supplied `UCX_NET_DEVICES` always takes precedence and is never overwritten. ### `ray/experimental/rdt/rdt_manager.py` `RDTManager.shutdown()` now calls `release_nic_for_current_actor()` to return the actor's NIC to the pool on clean shutdown. (Known gap: a SIGKILLed actor leaks its NIC until `release_all_for_node` is called — `snapshot()` gives operators visibility into this; a reaper is a natural follow-up.) ### `ray/tests/test_rdt_nic_allocator.py` (new) - `discover_rdma_nics` against a fake sysfs tree (parametrized: no devices / single device / multi-port / multi-device, verifying sorted determinism). - `NICAllocator` logic exercised directly as a plain class (no cluster): acquire/release cycle, exhaustion, re-entrancy, idempotent registration, unknown node, `release_all_for_node`. - Fail-open checks: flag unset, and flag set but no NICs discovered —both return `None` before any Ray call is made. - One end-to-end test with `ray_start_regular`: 4 actors contend for 2 fake NICs, exactly 2 succeed, and releasing one frees a slot for a waiter. ## Design notes / open questions carried from the issue discussion - **Opt-in and fail-open by design** — with `RAY_RDT_NIC_PINNING` unset, every code path here is a no-op; existing RDT/NIXL users see zero behavior change. - **Not scheduler-aware** — the allocator can refuse a NIC when the pool is exhausted, but it does not (and cannot, from application code) prevent Ray from *placing* another actor on an already-full node. That trade-off is what keeps this out of Ray Core for v1, per @stephanie-wang's suggestion. - **GPU/NIC PCIe affinity** (e.g. matching topology via `nvidia-smi topo -m`) is intentionally out of scope here — this PR only does exclusive assignment. Happy to iterate on affinity-aware allocation as a follow-up once the basic mechanism is validated. - **NIC granularity**: one allocatable unit = one (device, port) pair, not one HCA. Flagging this in case multi-port HCAs should be treated differently. ## Test plan - [x] New unit tests in `test_rdt_nic_allocator.py` (sysfs discovery, allocator logic, fail-open paths, end-to-end multi-actor contention) - [ ] Manual validation on real RDMA hardware (multi-NIC node) — checking `UCX_NET_DEVICES` is set correctly per actor and transfers no longer collide on one NIC - [x] Confirmed default behavior (flag unset) is unchanged for existing NIXL tests
signal.author: AyushKashyapII

signal.title: [core][raylet] Recompute OOM threshold on every poll so it tracks cgroup limit
signal.text: ## Description This PR fixes stale Ray OOM thresholds when the node/container memory limit changes at runtime, for example after Kubernetes in-place pod resize (IPPR) updates the cgroup memory limit. Previously, Ray cached the OOM threshold in multiple places from the memory limit observed at startup. If the limit later changed, the cached threshold could drift from the actual cgroup limit: - **Downsize:** the cached threshold can be too high, so Ray's ordered worker-killing path may fire too late and the kernel/cgroup OOM killer can kill the pod first. - **Upsize:** the cached threshold can be too low, so Ray can start killing workers before the newly granted memory budget is usable. This PR stops relying on a one-shot threshold value and recomputes the effective threshold from the latest memory snapshot / cgroup constraint at runtime. ## Changes - `ThresholdMemoryMonitor` no longer caches threshold bytes from startup. - It stores the threshold configuration inputs (`usage_threshold`, `min_memory_free_bytes`, resource isolation mode, and cgroup manager reference). - It recomputes the effective threshold on every poll so `memory.max` changes are reflected without restarting the raylet. - `TimeBasedWorkerKillingPolicy` is fixed together with the monitor. - `WorkerKillingPolicyFactory` no longer computes a one-shot threshold and passes it into the policy. - `TimeBasedWorkerKillingPolicy` now accepts a threshold getter and recomputes the threshold for each worker-killing decision using the latest `MemoryUsageSnapshot.total_bytes`. - Runtime threshold computation is made safe for repeated calls. - Added `MemoryMonitorUtils::GetMemoryThresholdOrNull()` for poll-time / decision-time use. - Unlike the startup-oriented `GetMemoryThreshold()`, this helper does not crash the raylet on transient cgroup read failures or temporary runtime states. - Resource isolation threshold handling is made safer. - Under resource isolation, `memory.high` is treated as the authoritative user-slice threshold. - If `memory.high` cannot be read or parsed, the current monitor poll / worker-killing decision is skipped. - This avoids falling back to a host-level threshold from `/proc/meminfo`, which can be much larger than the user- slice cap and can silently disable resource-isolation OOM protection. - Fixed related reliability issues found during review: - Avoid comparing memory usage against `kNull` thresholds. - Avoid invalid threshold fraction reporting when threshold resolution fails. - Ensure cgroup manager lifetime outlives the threshold monitor poll thread. - Make resource-isolation test fake cgroup managers outlive the monitor instance. - Add bounded waits and file I/O assertions to the runtime cgroup-resize regression test. ## Tests ```bash bazel build //src/ray/raylet:worker_killing_policy_factory bazel test \ //src/ray/common/tests:threshold_memory_monitor_test \ //src/ray/common/tests:memory_monitor_utils_test \ //src/ray/raylet/tests:worker_killing_policy_by_time_test Added/updated regression coverage includes: - TestThresholdTracksRuntimeCgroupLimitChanges - TestResourceIsolationThresholdReadFailureSkipsPoll - TestResourceIsolationInvalidThresholdSkipsPoll - TestPolicyRecomputesThresholdFromLatestTotalMemory - TestPolicySkipsWhenThresholdUnavailable ## Out of scope EventMemoryMonitor / cgroup memory.high re-application is still separate: resizing the host/container limit may require the cgroup manager to re-apply user-slice constraints. This PR focuses on ensuring Ray's threshold-monitor and time- based worker-killing policy consume the latest runtime threshold instead of stale startup values.

signal.title: [Data] Warn when configured memory is below 1.25x max USS
signal.text: ## Description Add an execution-end hook to the issue detector lifecycle. After a successful execution, the `high_memory_detector` warns for each map operator with an observed maximum USS when logical memory isn't configured or is less than 125% of that maximum. The warning shows the maximum worker memory, whether memory was configured, and an exact `memory=<bytes>` recommendation. ## Related issues closes #65511. ## Additional information The 125% comparison and recommendation use integer arithmetic, so I round up to a whole number of bytes. : ) ### Example warning ```text Operator 'Map(<lambda>)' used up to 8.0GiB of memory per worker. No logical memory was configured. To avoid out-of-memory errors, set memory=10737418240 (10.0GiB) in the appropriate function or method call. ```

signal.title: [Jobs] Guard recovered monitors against stale job state
signal.text: ## Summary Prevent recovered submission-job monitors from recreating deleted jobs or overwriting jobs that have already reached a terminal state. ## Problem `JobManager._recover_running_jobs()` schedules monitors asynchronously for non-terminal jobs. A job record can be deleted or transition to a terminal state between the recovery scan and the monitor's reconciliation pass. The existing monitor may then attempt to write `FAILED`: - If the record was deleted, `put_status()` may recreate it with `entrypoint="Entrypoint not found."`. - If the job is already terminal, the monitor may attempt an invalid or incorrect terminal-state transition. - A temporary `get_info()` failure for a `PENDING` job may be treated as a monitor failure instead of being retried. ## Changes - Stop monitoring immediately when the job record no longer exists. - Preserve terminal job states without writing another status. - Apply the same deleted/terminal checks in the monitor exception path. - Retry temporary `PENDING` job metadata-read failures on the next monitor iteration. - Add guarded status updates that require: - the job record to still exist; and - the current status to match the status observed by the monitor. - Stop the monitor when a guarded update loses a deletion or status race. - Add focused tests for deleted records, terminal transitions, temporary GCS failures, and guarded ## Related issues Fixes #65251 ## Additional information > Optional: Add implementation details, API changes, usage examples, screenshots, etc.

signal.title: [Core] Mobilint Accelerator Support
signal.text: ## Description This PR adds first-class support for Mobilint MBLT NPUs to Ray's accelerator abstraction by introducing a new `MBLTAcceleratorManager` under `ray/_private/accelerators/mblt.py`. This integration is developed and contributed by ETRI (Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute) in collaboration with Mobilint. Based on the SDKs provided by Mobilint, ETRI has implemented this software integration to align with Ray's official accelerator policies and architectural standards. The goal is to make MBLT resources natively schedulable in Ray (e.g., `resources={"MBLT": 1}`) and to provide per-worker/actor device isolation via a conventional "visible devices" environment variable, consistent with Ray's existing accelerator patterns (GPU, TPU, Neuron, etc.). **Key behaviors:** - Resource name: `MBLT` - Scheduling unit: Whole cards only (no fractional sharing). - Visibility isolation: Ray sets `MBLT_DEVICES` (comma-separated IDs) for worker/actor processes. - Runtime IDs: Users can access assigned IDs via `ray.get_runtime_context().get_accelerator_ids()`. ## Motivation Mobilint MBLT devices are increasingly utilized in heterogeneous clusters for specialized AI workloads. Currently, users must rely on custom resources and manual environment variable management to use these NPUs with Ray. This manual process is error-prone and breaks the seamless Ray-native experience. By introducing this PR, ETRI aims to provide a standardized interface for the MBLT lifecycle within the Ray ecosystem so that: - Ray's internal scheduler treats MBLT cards as first-class accelerators. - Cluster-wide resource management and isolation remains consistent across different hardware types. - Research and industrial users at ETRI and beyond can deploy MBLT-based workloads with minimal configuration. ## Usage example ```python import ray # Requesting 1 MBLT NPU card @ray.remote(resources={"MBLT": 1}) class MBLTWorker: def get_info(self): return ray.get_runtime_context().get_accelerator_ids() w = MBLTWorker.remote() # Expected output: {"MBLT": ["0"]} print(ray.get(w.get_info.remote())) ``` ## Contributors - Software Implementation: ETRI (Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute) - Hardware/SDK Support: Mobilint
signal.author: dataminsu

signal.title: Supporting Host Name routing rather than primarily relying on IP address/port
signal.text: ### Description Add a RAY_NODE_USE_HOSTNAME environment variable. When set to 1, Ray uses socket.gethostname() instead of an IP address for node identification. The node address is a string throughout the entire path (get_node_ip_address() → GCS registration → NodeInfo.node_manager_address → gRPC connections), so substituting a hostname at the entry point appears to propagate cleanly. In fact, we've POCd this with a Ray fork and it is working well. ### Use case Ray identifies nodes by IP address, and this convention propagates through to gRPC TLS handshakes, where certificate SANs are validated against the connection address. However, many organizational Certificate Authorities — including mine — issue certificates with hostname SANs only, not IP SANs. As a result, operators are forced to either stand up a separate private CA dedicated to Ray or disable TLS verification entirely — neither of which is great. I'd be happy to contribute this change upstream if the approach aligns with the project's direction. Additionally, I'd love to understand why Ray chose IP-based identification in the first place. There may be assumptions elsewhere in the system that I'm not seeing. Are there known cases where hostname resolution would break things? Thanks!
signal.author: shayansadeghieh

signal.title: Fix/tls server cert hot reload
signal.text: ## Description Fixes the **server-side** half of #65365. Ray's Python gRPC servers previously read TLS cert/key/CA files once at startup via `grpc.ssl_server_credentials()`. When cert-manager rotates files on disk (e.g. KubeRay mTLS), running servers kept presenting the old certificate until process restart. This PR switches `add_port_to_grpc_server()` to `grpc.dynamic_ssl_server_credentials()` with a `_ReloadableServerCertConfig` fetcher that: - Re-reads cert files when their mtimes change - Seeds the mtime cache after the initial load to avoid redundant reloads - Falls back to the last known-good configuration on stat/read/parse errors (raising from the fetcher would break new handshakes) **Affected Python gRPC servers:** Ray Client server, dashboard agent gRPC, Serve replica internal gRPC. ### Known gaps (out of scope) | Area | Status | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **Client/channel side** (`init_grpc_channel` in `grpc_utils.py`) | Not in this PR | Still reads TLS material once via `grpc.ssl_channel_credentials()`. Blocked on [grpc/grpc#41779](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/41779) — Python gRPC has no dynamic reload API for channels. | | **C++ core** (`src/ray/rpc/grpc_server.cc`) | Not in this PR | GCS, raylet, object manager, etc. load certs once at startup via `grpc::SslServerCredentials()`. Separate path, unaffected by this change. | ## Related issues Related to #65365 (server-side scope). ## Additional information ### Test plan - [x] `python -m pytest -v -s python/ray/_common/tests/test_tls_utils.py` — 7/7 passed (macOS) - [ ] `python -m pytest -v -s python/ray/tests/test_tls_auth.py::test_tls_server_cert_rotation_without_restart` — skipped locally on darwin; runs in CI on Linux - [x] `pre-commit run --from-ref master --to-ref HEAD` — passed ### Contribution notes - No duplicate open PR found for this change. - AI assistance was used; all changes reviewed by the submitter. - Every commit includes DCO `Signed-off-by`.
